provenance.paper_title: MMed-RAG: Versatile Multimodal RAG System for Medical Vision-Language Models

representation_paths.memory_component: domain-partitioned clinical-report knowledge base (radiology, ophthalmology, pathology report corpora built from dataset training splits), indexed by an image-text contrastive multimodal retriever

evidence.section: Full paper: Sec. 3.1 Domain-Aware Retrieval Mechanism; Sec. 3.2 Adaptive Retrieved Context Selection
evidence.figure_or_table: Algorithm 1 (retrieval step, line 23); Figure 2 system overview
evidence.paraphrase: The persistent store is a corpus of medical reports drawn from the training splits of five datasets, partitioned by medical domain. A BiomedCLIP-based domain-identification module labels the incoming medical image, which selects the corresponding domain-specific multimodal retriever; that retriever (ResNet-50 image encoder + BioClinicalBERT text encoder trained contrastively to align an image with its own report) embeds the query image and does similarity search over the report embeddings, returning top-k reports that are appended verbatim as context for the Med-LVLM. The stored items are natural-language report text, retrieved directly and read verbatim by the generator.

adjudication_notes: Full text read via arXiv HTML. Inclusion condition (a): the retrieval memory is the entire contribution, not an incidental context window. Condition (b): the non-text modality drives memory access -- the medical image is the retrieval query and also the signal for domain identification, and the retriever is trained on image-report alignment.

Tier: T1. The knowledge base, the domain classifier and the domain-specific retrievers are all frozen after construction; at inference the system only classifies the image and reads top-k. The adaptive retrieved-context selection (Sec. 3.2) varies how many retrieved contexts are used per query but is a query-conditioned read, not a persistent change to memory content, metadata, organization or policy, so it does not raise the tier.

Explicitly not T3: RAG-based preference fine-tuning (RAG-PT) constructs cross-modality and overall-alignment preference pairs and applies DPO to the Med-LVLM entirely offline before deployment (Algorithm 1). Per the guide, offline DPO never qualifies, and in any case it tunes the generator rather than a memory write/maintenance/retrieval policy.
No benchmark record: the paper evaluates on five pre-existing datasets (MIMIC-CXR, IU-Xray, Harvard-FairVLMed, PMC-OA, Quilt-1M; Table 8, Appendix A.2) and introduces no new benchmark.
